Subject: Draft review — 3 stars

Three stars. There’s a lot I genuinely like about my grooming van, but the way a plumbing failure was handled is why this isn’t a higher rating.

Harbourline did the fitout for my mobile dog grooming business. First, credit where it’s due: the stainless tub and ramp are honestly the best thing about the van. Dogs walk right in, and anything that makes getting a large dog into a bath less of a wrestling event is a win. I use this setup for work, not weekend trips, and those parts make my day easier.

On October 27, a fitting on the hot water line let go mid-groom. Water went across the floor and into the cabinet while I had Moose, a 110-pound Bernese, in the tub. Moose sat through the whole flood like a king surveying his waterfront property. Absolutely unbothered. I was the one screaming. He apparently thought we’d upgraded to a spa with an indoor water feature.

Funny now, considerably less funny while it was happening. I had to towel him off and send him home half done, then cancel the rest of that day. The van was off the road from October 27 to November 6, and I lost six more bookings as well as the remainder of the day it happened. For a mobile groomer, no working van means no working business.

The leak itself isn’t what bothered me most. Stuff breaks. What upset me was the response before anyone had inspected it. Glenn’s email said these lines don’t usually just let go and suggested the heater had been run dry or someone had been hanging things off the pipe, which would be user error and not covered. Neither had happened. The pipe was behind a cabinet door. Being met with possible blame before the problem had even been looked at was frustrating, especially with bookings to cancel.

The earliest appointment offered was November 3, with a $180 diagnostic fee. The invoice included a 12-month workmanship warranty excluding misuse or user error, so that initial response left me worried about how the warranty would actually be applied.

To be fair, Glenn did own it in the end. When the van was ready on November 6, he explained that a cheaper compression fitting had been substituted by his supplier and said that was on them. He replaced all the fittings on the hot side and refunded the $180 diagnostic charge. That matters, and I give him credit for taking responsibility and putting it right.

So this is a mixed review, not a “everything was terrible” review. Great tub and ramp, a plumbing failure that caused real downtime, and an initial response that made an already stressful situation harder than it needed to be. The eventual fix and refund were appreciated; I just wish we’d got to the “let’s investigate” stage without the user-error suggestion first.

For other groomers or trades considering a fitout, my advice is to get the warranty details in writing, including how diagnostic fees and possible user-error issues will be handled. I’m happy with some important parts of the build, but the after-sales experience is why I’m landing at three stars.
